title: The Resurrection and Commission
overview: Mark Chapter 16 narrates the pivotal resurrection of Jesus Christ, marking the triumph over death and the fulfillment of prophecy. The chapter begins with the women discovering the empty tomb and receiving the angelic announcement that Jesus has risen. It then recounts Jesus’ post-resurrection appearances to Mary Magdalene, two disciples, and the eleven apostles, emphasizing both belief and unbelief among His followers. The chapter concludes with the Great Commission, where Jesus commands His disciples to preach the gospel to all creation, promising signs that will accompany believers and His ascension into heaven. This chapter is foundational for Christian faith, affirming the resurrection as the cornerstone of salvation and the mandate for global evangelism.
structure:
**Verses 1-8: The Empty Tomb and Angelic Announcement.** The chapter opens with the women visiting Jesus’ tomb early on the first day of the week, discovering the stone rolled away and encountering a young man in white who announces Jesus’ resurrection and instructs them to inform the disciples.

**Verses 9-13: Jesus’ Post-Resurrection Appearances and Initial Unbelief.** Jesus first appears to Mary Magdalene, then to two disciples in another form, but the majority of the followers initially do not believe these reports.

**Verses 14-18: Jesus’ Appearance to the Eleven and the Great Commission.** Jesus reproves the apostles for their unbelief, commands them to preach the gospel worldwide, and promises miraculous signs that will accompany believers.

**Verses 19-20: The Ascension and the Apostles’ Ministry.** The chapter concludes with Jesus’ ascension to heaven and the apostles going forth to preach, empowered by the Lord and confirmed by accompanying signs.

keyVerses.text: And he saith unto them, Be not affrighted: Ye seek Jesus of Nazareth, which was crucified: he is risen; he is not here: behold the place where they laid him.
keyVerses.significance: This verse is central as it proclaims the resurrection of Jesus, the foundation of Christian hope and victory over death. It confirms that Jesus is alive, fulfilling His promise and Scripture, and it reassures believers not to fear.

keyVerses.text: And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.
keyVerses.significance: This command, known as the Great Commission, establishes the mission of the church to evangelize all nations. It underscores the universal scope of the gospel and the responsibility of believers to share the message of salvation.

keyVerses.text: He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned.
keyVerses.significance: This verse highlights the necessity of faith and baptism in the process of salvation, emphasizing the consequences of belief and unbelief. It encapsulates the gospel’s call to repentance and commitment.

keyVerses.text: So then after the Lord had spoken unto them, he was received up into heaven, and sat on the right hand of God.
keyVerses.significance: This verse affirms Jesus’ ascension and exaltation, signifying His divine authority and ongoing intercession for believers. It marks the transition from His earthly ministry to His heavenly reign.

characters.name: Mary Magdalene
characters.description: A devoted follower of Jesus who first discovers the empty tomb and witnesses the risen Christ. She plays a key role in announcing the resurrection to the disciples, symbolizing faithful witness and transformation.

characters.name: The Young Man in White
characters.description: An angelic figure present in the tomb who delivers the resurrection message to the women. He reassures them and directs them to inform the disciples, serving as a divine messenger.

characters.name: Jesus Christ
characters.description: The risen Lord who appears to His followers, reproves their unbelief, commissions them to preach the gospel, and ascends to heaven. His resurrection and ascension confirm His deity and the fulfillment of redemption.

characters.name: The Eleven Disciples
characters.description: The core group of Jesus’ followers who receive the Great Commission. They initially struggle with unbelief but are ultimately empowered to spread the gospel and confirm it with signs.

themes.description: The chapter centers on Jesus’ resurrection, affirming His victory over death and sin. This theme is foundational for Christian faith, demonstrating God’s power and the promise of eternal life.

The narrative contrasts belief and doubt among Jesus’ followers, highlighting the challenge of accepting the resurrection. It calls believers to trust in the risen Christ despite initial fears or skepticism.
The Great Commission commands the disciples to preach the gospel worldwide, establishing the church’s mission. This theme connects to the broader biblical call to make disciples of all nations.
Jesus’ ascension and seating at God’s right hand signify His sovereign authority and ongoing intercession. This theme assures believers of Christ’s exalted position and presence.

historicalContext: Mark’s Gospel was written in the first century AD, likely between 65-70 AD, during a time of Roman occupation in Palestine. The Jewish customs of Sabbath observance and burial practices, such as anointing the body with spices, are evident in the narrative. The political environment was tense, with Jewish resistance to Roman rule and messianic expectations high. The empty tomb and resurrection message would have been revolutionary, challenging both Jewish and Roman worldviews. The early Christian community faced persecution, making the resurrection a source of hope and empowerment for spreading the gospel.

theologicalInterpretations.description: This tradition emphasizes the sovereignty of God in the resurrection, viewing it as the definitive proof of Christ’s deity and the basis for justification by faith. The Great Commission is seen as a mandate for faithful proclamation grounded in God’s grace.

Dispensationalists interpret the resurrection as a literal, bodily event inaugurating the current church age. The signs mentioned are understood as gifts accompanying believers, and the Great Commission is linked to the church’s distinct role before Christ’s second coming.

Early church writers like Augustine and Chrysostom highlight the resurrection as the cornerstone of Christian hope and the defeat of death. They stress the importance of faith and baptism as means of grace and the continuation of Christ’s work through the apostles.

crossReferences.connection: Paul affirms the resurrection of Christ as the gospel’s foundation, paralleling Mark’s emphasis on Jesus rising on the third day.
The promise of the Holy Spirit empowering believers to witness globally complements Jesus’ Great Commission in Mark 16.
Paul explains baptism as a symbol of being united with Christ in His death and resurrection, echoing Mark 16:16’s connection between belief, baptism, and salvation.
Luke’s account of Jesus’ post-resurrection appearances aligns with Mark’s narrative, providing additional details about the disciples’ reactions and commissioning.
This verse describes Jesus’ exaltation at God’s right hand, paralleling Mark 16:19’s depiction of the ascension.

application: Trust in the risen Christ as the foundation of your faith, overcoming doubt and fear.
Obey the Great Commission by actively sharing the gospel with those around you and beyond.
Embrace baptism as a public declaration of faith and a step toward salvation.
Rely on God’s power and presence, knowing that signs and wonders can confirm the gospel message.
Live with the assurance of Christ’s ascension and ongoing intercession on your behalf.
Respond to unbelief in yourself and others with patience, prayer, and faithful witness.
conclusion: Mark Chapter 16 stands as a powerful testament to the resurrection of Jesus Christ, the cornerstone of Christian belief and hope. It reveals the transformative power of encountering the risen Lord, challenges believers to overcome doubt, and commissions the church to proclaim the gospel universally. The chapter’s themes of resurrection, faith, mission, and divine authority continue to inspire and equip Christians to live boldly in obedience and confidence. Its enduring message calls every believer to trust in Christ’s victory, participate in His mission, and live under His sovereign reign.
timeline: c. AD 30-33 - Resurrection and Ascension of Jesus Christ

outline.heading: The Women Visit the Tomb
outline.description: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome come early to anoint Jesus’ body but find the stone rolled away and encounter a young man in white, signaling the resurrection.

outline.heading: The Angel’s Resurrection Announcement
outline.description: The angel tells the women not to fear and announces that Jesus is risen, instructing them to tell the disciples and Peter that Jesus will meet them in Galilee.

outline.heading: Jesus’ Appearances and Disciples’ Unbelief
outline.description: Jesus appears first to Mary Magdalene and then to two disciples, but many of the followers do not believe the reports of His resurrection.

outline.heading: Jesus Reproves and Commissions the Eleven
outline.description: Jesus confronts the disciples’ unbelief, commands them to preach the gospel to all creation, and promises signs that will accompany believers.

outline.heading: The Ascension and Apostolic Ministry
outline.description: Jesus ascends to heaven and sits at God’s right hand, while the apostles go forth preaching everywhere, empowered by the Lord and confirmed by miraculous signs.
